content: Jane E. Henney was appointed by President Bill Clinton and served as the Commissioner of the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) from 1998 to 2001. Prior to this role, she worked at the FDA from 1992 to 1994 as the Deputy Commissioner for Operations under then-Commissioner David Aaron Kessler, MD. After her initial tenure at the FDA, she held the position of Vice President of the Health Sciences Center at the University of New Mexico (UNM). Jane Henney was born in Woodburn, Indiana. She completed her undergraduate education at Manchester College and earned her MD degree from the Indiana University School of Medicine. She pursued postgraduate training at The University of Texas MD Anderson Cancer Center in Houston, Texas. Trained as a medical oncologist, she joined the National Cancer Institute (NCI) at the National Institutes of Health (NIH) in 1976, where she worked in the Cancer Therapy and Evaluation Program. She is married to James Robert Graham III, MD, who has also had a distinguished career as a physician and leader in the medical field. After leaving the FDA, she joined the board of directors of the pharmaceutical company AstraZeneca. In 2003, she was appointed Senior Vice President and Provost for Health Affairs at the University of Cincinnati.
